title: Was it really a revolution? From steam to silicon

review.note: Built from Mr Garry's own lessons for this unit (2026–27 scheme of work). Check wording against the lesson PowerPoints before relying on it.

learn.intro: Time to judge. This topic brings the whole unit together with the Revolution Tracker, prepares you for the Harkness debate, then applies the same criteria to the Internet and to AI, including what the Industrial Revolution can teach us about the UAE's future.

sections.title: 1. Was it really a revolution?

blocks.p: Use the four criteria (Scale, Speed, Depth, Duration) to compare very different changes fairly. Change that looks dramatic on one criterion can look less revolutionary on another:

ul: Urbanisation scores very high on Scale (millions moved) but more moderately on Speed within one town (growth over decades).
A single invention such as the power loom had narrow immediate Scale but very high Depth for the workers it replaced.
Agricultural change was slower, but it was a precondition for everything else.

blocks.p: Not every area of life changed equally. Some things showed continuity, such as the monarchy, many rural ways of life and religious practice. A strong judgement shows this unevenness rather than claiming "everything changed".

evidence: Compare developments on all four criteria, not just one.

blocks.p: Assessment proposition: "The Industrial Revolution changed the world more profoundly than the revolutions that followed it." How far do you agree?

A Harkness discussion is student-led and evidence-based. The teacher observes. You are marked on Knowledge, Precise evidence, Historical reasoning, Responding/building/challenging, and a short written Final judgement (4 marks each, 20 in total).
Prepare an Evidence Bank: your three strongest pieces of evidence, one counterargument to your own view, and two questions to ask classmates. Do not script a speech.

ul: Agree with nuance: "I agree to some extent, but the evidence from… suggests…"

sections.title: 3. From steam to silicon: the Internet and AI

blocks.p: Key milestones: ARPANET sent the first message between computers in 1969; Tim Berners-Lee's World Wide Web became publicly available in 1991, making the Internet usable by non-specialists; e-commerce, search and social media spread from the mid-1990s; the smartphone era (often dated from the iPhone in 2007) made constant mobile access normal for billions.
Compare with the criteria: the Internet spread globally in roughly 20–30 years (Speed) to billions (Scale). Its Depth is huge, but its Duration cannot yet be judged with hindsight.
Mechanisation mainly replaced physical tasks; automation and AI increasingly perform cognitive tasks too, a significant difference.

The UAE is pursuing rapid economic and technological change, diversifying beyond oil and investing in education, innovation and AI, while emphasising heritage, community and national identity. History teaches caution: people in 1750 could not predict 1900, so we should be careful about confident predictions about AI.

exam.criteria_note: Practice questions written for this unit. AI feedback is formative only (no marks) until department KS3 criteria are added.

questions.label: Teacher-created practice question
questions.q: "The Industrial Revolution changed the world more profoundly than the revolutions that followed it." How far do you agree? (Harkness final judgement, about 150–200 words)
questions.asks: Write a short, qualified final judgement using your strongest evidence and the four criteria, comparing with the Internet or AI.
steps: Use your strongest evidence, naming criteria.
Conclude on which criteria decide it.
questions.plan: 3 minutes planning from your Evidence Bank, 10 minutes writing, 2 minutes checking qualifiers.

model.t: The Industrial Revolution changed the world considerably more profoundly than later revolutions, to a large extent, because its depth of change was unmatched.

It transformed where people lived and how they worked: Manchester grew from around 18,000 people in the 1750s to over 300,000 by 1850, and new public health laws such as the 1848 Act changed the relationship between government and citizens.
However, the Internet and AI may prove faster and larger in scale, even if their depth and duration cannot yet be judged with hindsight.
Therefore the Industrial Revolution's profundity lies in its depth and its now-provable duration, an advantage later, still-unfolding revolutions cannot yet claim.

full: P: The Industrial Revolution changed the world more / less profoundly, to a large / some extent, because…
E: However, the Internet / AI… in terms of speed / scale…
J: Therefore, overall… because the deciding criterion is…

E: precise evidence (name, date, number, source)
